rationale: Motor terminals connect to the driver outputs.
The harness is wired to the motor.
The harness is wired to the driver outputs.
The driver takes its supply from the main rail.
The regulator takes its input from the main rail.
The rail is fed by the battery.
The controller is supplied by the regulator.
The controller sends commands to the driver.
The motor shaft drives the wheel.
The motor is bolted to the bracket.
The bracket is bolted to the chassis.
Motor speed sets the top speed.
Motor power draw sets the runtime.
Battery energy sets the runtime.
Driver limits are part of the electrical requirement.
Battery limits are part of the electrical requirement.
Regulator limits are part of the electrical requirement.
Wiring limits are part of the electrical requirement.
The chassis is the largest mass item.
Motor behaviour is checked under load.
Motor fit is checked at assembly.
Bracket fit is checked at assembly.
